newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC said expecting reduced French wheat yield.
newsitem.headline: ONIC said expecting reduced French wheat yield.

text.p: France's grain office ONIC expects the 1997 soft wheat crop to achieve an average yield of 6.9 tonnes per hectare against 7.3 tonnes last year, grain industry sources on Friday.
The office is also targeting a barley yield of 5.8 tonnes per hectare against 6.25 tonnes last year and a sharp fall in the durum wheat yield to 3.6 tonnes from 4.65 tonnes.
The forecast drafted on June 19 from data collected by ONIC's regional offices has not yet been officially released.
ONIC officials could not be reached for comment.
ONIC is widely expected to release its first estimate for the 1997/98 grain crop next Wednesday.

Using the latest estimates released by ONIC on June 11 of 1997 sowings of 4.95 milllion hectares, this would put the 1997 soft wheat crop at 34.2 million tonnes against a record 34.7 million last year. Based on sowings of 1.611 million ha, the barley crop would reach 9.34 million tonnes against 9.54 million last year. The durum wheat crop would fall to 924,624 tonnes from 1.255 million using a sowings figure of 256,840 ha.
"At this stage the crop potential is very strong" one source said, adding the first cuts in the southwest showed good specific weight.
Rains in May and June allowed the soft wheat and barley crops to recoup losses linked to dry conditions in March and April. But the rain came too late for the durum wheat crop in southern France.
Continued wet weather is, however, raising fears that the soft wheat crop's protein content could be hit.
